<meta>Running header: 金剛經口訣 (Oral Explanation of the Diamond Sutra); page number 七九 (79). Sutra text alternates with Huineng's commentary.</meta>"Subhuti, what do you think? If someone filled the <term>trichiliocosm</term> <gloss>the 'three-thousand great-thousand world system,' a whole Buddhist universe</gloss> with the <term>seven treasures</term> <gloss>gold, silver, lapis, crystal and other precious substances</gloss> and gave them all away in charity, would this person, through this cause, gain much merit?"

"Yes indeed, World-Honored One. Through this cause this person would gain a very great deal of merit."

"Subhuti, if merit had real substance, the <term>Tathagata</term> <gloss>'Thus-Come One,' a title of the Buddha</gloss> would not speak of gaining much merit. It is because merit is without substance that the Tathagata speaks of gaining much merit."

The merit of the seven treasures cannot bring about the fruit of Buddhahood, <term>bodhi</term> <gloss>awakening</gloss>; that is why it is called "without substance." Because it cannot be bounded by any measure or number, it is called "much." But if one is able to pass beyond it, then one no longer speaks of "much."

**Section Twenty: Leaving Behind Form, Leaving Behind Marks** The three bodies <note>the Buddha's three bodies: the Dharma body, the reward body and the transformation body</note> are fully complete, and all the marks are perfectly fulfilled; yet when persons and dharmas are both forgotten, this is "not complete." Therefore it is followed by the section on leaving behind form and leaving behind marks.

"Subhuti, what do you think? Can the Buddha be seen by means of a perfectly complete physical body?"

"No, World-Honored One. The Tathagata

<summary>This page concludes Section Nineteen of the Diamond Sutra, where the Buddha teaches that merit from lavish giving is called "much" precisely because it lacks real substance, with Huineng's comment that such merit cannot produce awakening. It then opens Section Twenty, which asks whether the Buddha can be seen through a perfect physical body.</summary>
